heading: Designs for plan 7
intro:
Everything you can see before it's built: the UI polish from your ten points, and three moon themes you could switch between or mix. Every design went through the realism supervisor (light, shadow, reflection, colour) and a design critic, and was fixed until approved. Nothing here is in the plugin yet.

Open the live mock ↗ A working copy of the Journal window with the plan 7 layer. Switch Full, Quiet and Plain, open the filter drawer, hover the rail, and press “Complete a quest” for the meteor. Try the moon themes there too: pick Ishgard Glass, Aether Crystal or Orrery, or choose Mix… to set a moon for each state. Pick “1.13” to compare with today.

groups.title: UI polish
groups.note: Your points 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8. Every image is a 1:1 crop of the mock at Full, Quiet and Plain, next to 1.13 as shipped.

items.name: Bigger headings and column headers
items.alt: Full in 1.13 and in v7: the whole window, then the quest-pane headings and Journal header at 1:1
items.pitch: Requirements, Rewards, Unlocks, Moonlit and Path become a real Section heading at 1.80× body (tapering to 1.60× at 150% scale), in the game font with a brass rule. The Journal's column headers grow to 1.55× with brighter ink and a taller header row, never larger than the group headers.
changes: Section role 1.80× body (was the caption size); the hero title stays the largest
Column headers 1.55×, +0.08 em tracking, Secondary ink, header row 30 px at Full
Quiet and Plain get the same steps in their own style
Follows Text size like every other role

items.name: The filter drawer, redesigned
items.alt: The filter drawer: 1.13 as shipped, then Full, Quiet and Plain, Advanced collapsed and expanded
items.pitch: Same place, same fade, same pin. It now fits the tree column exactly and sizes to its content, so there's no empty grey and nothing from the tree shows at the edges. A real header (“Filters”, a count of what's on, pin and close), sections in the heading style, moon toggles, and seven summary lines when Advanced is closed so you can see every setting at a glance.
changes: Exactly the tree column's width; the tree fades out underneath, so no text bleeds through
Sized to content, capped at the window; the footer stays when it scrolls
Title in the Title role with a “3 on” pill
Reset is a quiet text action with an 8-second Undo
Full: raised sheet with a brass edge; Quiet: flat and silver; Plain: ledger bands

items.name: A fuller rail with better motion
items.alt: The 1.13 rail and the v7 rail at each look, every station state at 2×, and the motion table
items.pitch: Icons go from 22 to 30 px, and the stations share the rail's height so it fills the bar. The brass thread between icons is gone. Hovering lifts the icon 2 px over a soft plate. Selecting one fades its plate in while a bead glides down the left edge to it.
changes: Icons 30 px (Full), 28 (Quiet), 20 (Plain)
Stations grow to share the rail, with room left for stars
No coloured lines between icons
Hover 0.12 s rise; select 0.15 s; the bead travels in 0.22 s; Reduce motion lands at once
Labels never move; only their colour changes

items.name: Better stars
items.alt: The 1.13 sky and the v7 sky: three depths, four temperatures, the twinkle curve, the constellations and the meteor
items.pitch: Stars at three depths, in four real star temperatures, each twinkling on its own slow curve. A constellation for each region (the Chocobo for A Realm Reborn, the Tower for Ishgard…) hides in the empty sky. Finishing a quest sends one meteor across. Stars only ever sit in empty sky, never under text.
changes: Far, mid and near stars, the near ones with a 5 px cross
Blue-white to amber temperatures
Six region constellations
A completion meteor, off with Reduce motion
Optional Milky Way, off by default
watch: Your call: turn the Milky Way on by default?
Your call: is the Chocobo right for A Realm Reborn?

items.name: Completed moon: darker seas, soft glow
items.alt: The shipped and v7 Completed medals at 16, 20, 32, 64 and 128 px, enlarged, and in table rows
items.pitch: The maria are a darker basalt with deeper hearts, and a faint cool glow sits around the moon. The craters you asked to darken show at 96 and 128 px, where they read as craters. Below that they would speckle, so small sizes keep the darker seas without them.
changes: Maria in basalt #56658C at 1.6× the opacity
Darker hearts in Imbrium, Serenitatis and Procellarum
Cool glow on every size
Craters at 96/128 px only, per the supervisor
Still 0.73× Ready, so it stays the quieter state

groups.title: Moon themes
groups.note: Your point 7. Three earlier concepts, rebuilt and improved, to sit beside Menphina's Medallion. Every theme uses the same shapes and meanings, so you can switch the whole look or mix and match: one theme's moon for each state, any theme's frames, and any colour palette. Try them in the live mock ↗

items.name: Ishgard Glass
items.alt: Ishgard Glass: the eight states at 16 to 96 px, on daylight, and in greyscale
items.pitch: Every moon is a stained-glass window in lead and stone, lit from behind like the Foundation's cathedral. Ready shows the Ishgard skyline on a moonlit shore; Blocked is glass cloud; Completed is the moon's face in four leaded panes; Locked out is a broken window. The critic ranked it first: “the most FFXIV of the set.”
changes: Backlit glass; only lead, stone and gilt catch front light
Skyline on Ready at hero size; at night on In journal
Flat two-tone glass clouds for Blocked
Faces split from frames, so they mix with any theme

more.cap: Mix proof: Glass moons in Medallion's frames and the reverse.

items.name: Aether Crystal
items.alt: Aether Crystal: the eight states at 16 to 96 px, on daylight, and in greyscale
items.pitch: The moon as cut moonstone in a silver 16-sided setting: facets catch the light, and aether glows through the stone. Blocked hides behind a faceted frost bank; Completed has a two-facet gilt check.
changes: Low-chroma moonstone silver frames
A 7-facet cut at row size, so small icons stay clean
Ready keeps the shared gilt so it always leads
Faces split from frames

more.cap: Mix proof: Crystal moons in Silver and Brass frames, Medallion moons in the Silver frame, and the kit.

items.name: Astrologian's Orrery
items.alt: Astrologian's Orrery: the eight states at 16 to 96 px, on daylight, and in greyscale
items.pitch: Remade so it's more than Medallion with stars: engraved silver moons in a brass astrolabe, with star charts on the dark sides. Ready is a dawn sighting with a limb scale, Done a graduated arc, and Dalamud glows rose.
changes: Engraved hatching at large sizes only, smooth below
Patinated brass cloud over a true new moon for Blocked
A graduated scale for Done
Faces split from frames

The Astrolabe frame kit: four tiers at Full and Quiet, the badge rings and the glyphs.

supervisor.summary:
The supervisor checks rendered images, never source, against one rule: light, shadow, reflection, colour and material must be believable, even in stylised art. A critic judged taste and identity.

  • UI: two rounds. The Completed moon's craters show only at 96 and 128 px, so small sizes never look like cheese. The drawer's shadows share one light. The rail lost its glow. The stars got a shorter near-star cross and a brighter meteor head.
  • Astrologian's Orrery: remade for its own identity, then two rounds. The engraved hatching is kept to large sizes, and Blocked's edge matches Medallion.
  • Aether Crystal: two rounds. The frost bank no longer outshines the moon, and the setting is now low-chroma silver.
  • Ishgard Glass: two rounds. Backlit flat glass with front-lit lead, and Locked out's hole rebuilt as broken panes.
  • Every theme passes the legibility checks at 16 px in greyscale: the weakest pair is at least 12, Ready leads by at least 1.3×, and Completed is at most 0.8× Ready.
